en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Sandals, 96.
The Training Rule on the *Asaṅkaccika*.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī entered a village for alms without wearing her inner robe (saṅkaccikā).
A whirlwind lifted up her outer robes (saṅghāṭī) on the street.
People raised a clamor.
“The lady’s breasts and hips are beautiful.
Being thus mocked by those men, that bhikkhunī became dejected.
Then, having gone to her dwelling, she reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were modest … [as above] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can a bhikkhunī enter a village without wearing her sarong? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī entered a village without wearing her sarong?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, bhikkhus, can a bhikkhunī enter a village without wearing her upper robe? …”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:
‘If any bhikkhunī should enter a village without wearing her chest-cloth, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such...
"nun" means... [as before].
... pe ... in this context, "nun" (bhikkhunī) is intended in this sense.
"Without a waist-cloth" (asaṅkaccikā) means without a saṅkaccika.
"Saṅkaccika" means that which is below the collarbone and above the navel; it is for the purpose of concealing that.
"Should enter a village" means...
For one who crosses the boundary of an enclosed village, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
For one who enters the precinct of an unenclosed village, there is an offense of expiation.
There is no offense—
For one whose robe has been torn away,
for one whose robe has been lost,
and for one who is ill.
through forgetfulness, through lack of knowledge,
or in times of misfortune.
"Of one who is insane,
of one who is a first-offender.
The thirteenth training rule is concluded.
The Ninth Chapter on Sandals.
The Chapter on Dhammika.
The Training Rule for Nanda.
Venerable ladies, the one hundred and sixty-six rules on expiation have been recited.
In this regard, I ask the venerable ladies:
"Are you pure in this matter?"
A second time I ask:
"Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask:
“Are you pure in this matter?
“The venerable ones are pure in this matter; therefore they are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The Minor Section is concluded.
The section on offenses entailing expiation (pācittiya) in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga is concluded.
